---
title: "Configuration"
---

A dataset's configuration is `tether.toml` at the dataset root, committed with
the manifests and loaded into `RepoConfig`. Every key but `[dataset] id` has a
default; a minimal file is `[tether] version = 2` plus the id `init` generates.
A dataset whose version is older than this tether's is refused by every
command except `tether upgrade`, which brings it forward one migration at a
time (see the [CLI guide](06-cli.qmd#upgrade)).

```toml
[tether]
version = 2         # the format this tether writes; older datasets need `tether upgrade`

[dataset]
id = "0a1b2c3d"      # 8 hex chars; the namespace of this dataset's pins and branches in every store

[snapshot]
auto = true          # CLI status/commit fingerprint by default (--no-snapshot wins)

[verify]
on_status = false    # also run a cheap verify of each committed object in status

[new]
auto_fork = false    # commit re-runs `new` from the pins it just created
fork = "lazy"        # "lazy": create a working branch on first writable open; "eager": during `new`

[defaults]           # policy for objects added without an explicit one
write = "fork"       # fork | track
file = "immutable"   # immutable | versioned
pin = "native"       # native | record

[vcs]
prefer = "jj"        # which adapter to use when both .jj and .git exist
# jj_path = "/opt/jj/bin/jj"
# git_path = "/usr/bin/git"

[backends.file]      # passed verbatim to the backend factory; one table per kind
storage_options = { region = "us-west-2" }

[backends.neon]
api_key_env = "NEON_API_KEY"

[backends.ducklake]
init_sql = ["CREATE SECRET (TYPE S3, PROVIDER credential_chain)"]
```

## Dataset id

`init` generates `[dataset] id`, and because `tether.toml` is committed every
clone shares it. Every native ref tether creates carries it -- pins are
`tether.<id>.<hash>`, working branches `tether.ws.<id>.<workspace>.<key>` --
and `gc` only considers refs in that namespace, so several datasets can share
one Icechunk repo or Neon project without being able to delete each other's
pins. Do not change it once anything has been committed: pins and branches
made under the old id are no longer recognised as this dataset's (`gc` treats
them as foreign and leaves them alone; `repair` recreates the pins the
manifests name under the new id). Datasets from before the id existed get one
from `tether upgrade`, which also renames their refs and rewrites history to
match. A fork of the repository that is meant to become an *independent*
dataset should change the id before it pins anything, or the two will share a
namespace and be able to `gc` each other again.

## Policies

A `Policy` is stored per object (`[policy]` in its manifest) and set with the
`--write`, `--file`, `--pin` options of `tether add` or `Repo.add(policy=...)`.

| Field | Values | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `write` | `fork` (default), `track` | `fork`: `new` creates a fresh per-workspace branch off the pin. `track`: the working ref is the locator's branch (e.g. `main`); use for production branches that must not be forked. |
| `file` | `immutable` (default), `versioned` | `file` backend only. `immutable`: any drift is an error at `status`. `versioned`: a single object in a versioning-enabled bucket/container is Addressable through its version id. |
| `pin` | `native` (default), `record` | Any backend. `record` drops `PIN`: `commit` records the state without creating a native ref, and `new` forks straight from the recorded state. Cheaper (no tag/branch per commit, nothing for `gc` to release) but recoverable only while the system retains that state -- `verify` reports `missing` once it is gone. See [Reclaiming storage](05-reclaiming-storage.qmd). |

## Import query

`[import] query` is the default SQL for `tether import` when neither `--table`
nor `--query` is given. It must yield tether's canonical columns (`key`,
`kind`, `uri` / `locator_json`, optional `policy_*`, `at`); the source (DSN or
file) is still passed on the command line, so no credentials land in the repo.
See [Registries and SQL](09-registries-and-sql.qmd).

```toml
[import]
query = "SELECT 'zarr/' || name AS key, 'icechunk' AS kind, uri FROM catalog WHERE format = 'icechunk'"
```

## Backend options

`[backends.<kind>]` is handed to the backend when it is first used. Only
non-secret settings belong here (regions, endpoints, environment-variable
*names*); credentials come from the environment. The per-backend keys are
listed in [Backends](08-backends.qmd).

## Workspace state

`.tether/workspace.toml` is untracked (ignored by the `.tether/.gitignore` that
`init` writes, alongside the operation log `.tether/ops.jsonl`) and is per
checkout / per jj workspace:

```toml
workspace_id = "7c1e0a4d9b2e4f6a8c1d3e5f7a9b0c2d"
last_snapshot_at = "2026-09-04T22:10:03.118Z"

[working_refs]                       # branches that exist
"zarr/imaging" = "tether.ws.0a1b2c3d.7c1e0a4d.zarr-imaging-3fa1c0"
"db/metrics" = "tether.ws.0a1b2c3d.7c1e0a4d.db-metrics-77e21d"

[pending_forks]                      # decided by `new`, created on first writable open
"features" = "tether.ws.0a1b2c3d.7c1e0a4d.features-9b2e4f"

[base_states."zarr/imaging"]         # committed state this working ref corresponds to
snapshot_id = "K3F7Q2ZJ1XN4Y8W0"     #   (differs from the manifest => stale)

[fork_points."zarr/imaging"]         # base state when the branch was forked (for promote)
snapshot_id = "K3F7Q2ZJ1XN4Y8W0"

[last_snapshot."zarr/imaging"]
snapshot_id = "K3F7Q2ZJ1XN4Y8W0"
```

`base_states` drive stale-working-copy detection (per object); `working_refs`
are what `open` writes to; `pending_forks` are the branches `new` decided on but has not
created (the first writable `open` moves an entry to `working_refs`);
`last_snapshot` is what `--no-snapshot` reuses.

## Operation log

`.tether/ops.jsonl` sits next to `workspace.toml`, equally untracked and
per workspace: one JSON object per line for every command that wrote to a
store -- the plan it applied, what it did (`result`), and what it replaced
(`pre`: the workspace state and VCS position before a `new`, the heads of
branches it reset, the manifests an `import` rewrote, the base heads a
`promote` moved from). `tether ops` reads it; `tether undo` reverses entries
from it and appends its own entry plus a one-line *mark*
(`{"undone": ID, "by": UNDO_ID}`) -- the file is only ever appended to, so an
interruption loses at most the line being written. Deleting the file loses
nothing but the ability to undo what came before.

## Environment variables

| Variable | Read by |
| --- | --- |
| `TETHER_REV` | `Repo.open` / `tether open` default revision |
| `NEON_API_KEY` (or `[backends.neon] api_key_env`) | neon |
| `DOLT_PASSWORD`, `DOLT_USER` (or `password_env` / `user_env`) | dolt |
| AWS / GCP / Azure credential chains | file (obstore), icechunk, delta, lance |
| `LAKECTL_*` or `~/.lakectl.yaml` | lakefs |
| pyiceberg catalog properties / env | iceberg |
